content.comment_body: Hello everyone, Here's my issue: I want to manage as many outputs as possible on several [product_name] modules using my main module's web page as a server. With the maximum network setup of 64 outputs (I believe), I'm unable to control all outputs because only 56 memory locations are available. I tried using the 'V' block on the web editor, but it didn’t work as expected, possibly because I misunderstood how this block works. How do I connect this 'V' block to my logic so all outputs can be controlled via switches? Is the maximum setup 16 expansion modules added to the main module, giving 17 in total and 68 outputs, or is it 16 modules overall (64 outputs)? If the 'V' block isn’t a solution, how can I manage all outputs from one web page using switches? Thanks so much for your input! [user_name]

Are you reading the respective V-bit with a digital network input? The extended web server only communicates with the [product_name] it’s installed on. In this scenario, that’s your 'main module.' So, you’ll need to forward the relevant V-bits to your other modules as required.
I've created a program for this (it's included in the zip file).

Give this a try. Why did you set the subnet mask to 255.255.255.128? Why not 255.255.255.0? I've changed it. If all devices are in the same subnet, you do not need to set a gateway address. I've removed it.
I'm not sure why I made that change, but okay. Everything is working now! Thanks for your assistance.

analysis.insight_summary: The user faced difficulty controlling many outputs across multiple [product_name] devices from a single web interface due to unclear network limits and confusion about using software blocks like the 'V' block. Guidance from the forum clarified network settings and how to distribute control bits, resulting in a functional solution.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants to control all outputs on multiple [product_name] devices through one central web page with easy network configuration and the ability to use available software blocks efficiently.
